name: The Autograph Tree

location.address: Walled Garden, Coole Park Nature Reserve, Gort, Co. Galway

official_register.name: Heritage Trees of Ireland (Tree Council of Ireland), record 221, Named trees, Fagus sylvatica Atropurpurea Group, recorded 18/09/2009 by Aubrey Fennell

access: Free. Coole Park Nature Reserve (NPWS) grounds open daily, 8:00-19:30 summer, 8:00-18:00 winter per the park's own page; free parking at the visitor centre (visitor centre open April to September). The tree stands just inside/beyond the red gates of the walled garden.
transport: Rural: about 4 km from Gort by road; Bus Eireann route 434 / Gort town then taxi or car; roughly 50-70 min door to door from Galway city (Aug 2026 check in CURATION-2026-08).
verify_notes: Species: coolepark.ie says mature copper beech already mature when Yeats carved his initials in 1898 at Lady Gregory's request; Wikipedia: initials of Yeats, Edward Martyn, Shaw, Synge, Rossi, Sean O'Casey. thisisgalway.ie (23 Apr 2025, updated 5 Feb 2026) lists Yeats, Synge, O'Casey, Shaw, Spicer-Simson, Countess of Cromartie, Elinor Monsell, Jack B. Yeats, Lady Gregory; calls it about 200 years old and 'just beyond the red gates of the Walled Garden'. Age: no figure from the owner; register band 150-200 in 2009 (so roughly 165-215 now); the 160 vs 200 year figures in popular pages are unsourced. Alive: Coole page modified 2026-03-17 still presents it; thisisgalway.ie article 2025/2026; an unverified older page mentions a protective fence around the trunk (not confirmed by the park page; enclosure open/closed unknown, treat access as 'view from the fence if needed'). A plaque at the base helps identify the carvings; some are fading as the bark heals (coolepark.ie). Pin: register record 221 at 53.09508,-8.8361 (precision 100 m) lies 20 m from the NIAH walled garden centroid (Reg 30412205, ITM-converted 53.09527,-8.83628), so it is the walled-garden beech; NIAH lists 'Autograph Tree' inside the garden. Discover Ireland's map link (53.09256,-8.83795) is the visitor centre, not the tree. No tree girth/height published. Recognition line candidate: the purple-leaved beech inside the walled garden whose bark holds the carved initials of Irish Revival writers, with a plaque at its base. Story hooks: Yeats carved first in 1898; the signatures are history, never an invitation to carve or touch. Also in walled garden (not separate trees): row of upright Irish yews (female clones) sheltering hothouses. Official source = owner of ground (NPWS). Fully free; 'flagged' not needed.
